public_primary_sources.claim_bound: CIDv1 is version varint + content-type multicodec + multihash; the maintained specification gives raw(0x55)+sha2-256 as an exact-byte example and states the multihash is hash-code + digest-length + digest.
Registry entries observed: cidv1 0x01 permanent; sha1 0x11 permanent; sha2-256 0x12 permanent; raw 0x55 permanent raw binary; git-raw 0x78 permanent Raw Git object.

derivation: If the addressed block bytes are exactly the canonical Git object hash preimage already named by the predecessor frontier, then the SHA-1 digest field in the CID multihash is the same 20-byte digest as the legacy Git object ID by hash-input identity.
The CID itself is not the Git object ID: CIDv1 adds version, codec, multihash-code and digest-length fields.

For raw(0x55)+sha1(0x11) with a 20-byte digest, the binary CID is 24 bytes before any textual multibase encoding, versus a 20-byte bare Git SHA-1 digest; identifier wrapper overhead is therefore 4 bytes in binary form.
Using raw avoids a mandatory payload transformation at the CID layer: the content type is registered as raw binary, so the addressed payload may remain the exact preimage bytes.
